title: Actuarial Statistics and Mathematical Demography
curriculum_locator: Stat H-306 Actuarial Statistics & Stat H-312 Actuarial Lab / Mathematical Demography; University of Dhaka four-year B.S. Honours Statistics curriculum, starting session 2023–2024

units.title: Theory of Interest, Discount Rates & Financial Mathematics
scope: The economic principle of the time value of money: capital accumulation, compound interest vs simple interest, and accumulation functions a(t)
Effective annual rate of interest i, discount factor v = 1/(1+i), and effective rate of discount d = i/(1+i) = 1 - v
Nominal rates of interest i^(m) and nominal discount rates d^(m) compounded m-thly, and their asymptotic limits as m -> infinity
The instantaneous force of interest delta(t) = a'(t)/a(t), relation to constant discount delta = ln(1+i), and continuous accumulation factors
Equations of value, yield rates, Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Net Present Value (NPV), and uniqueness of rates under Descartes' Rule of Signs
Real vs nominal rates of interest, Fisher's inflation equation, and duration and convexity of fixed-income cash flows

units.title: Annuities Certain, Varying Cash Flows & Loan Amortization Mechanics
scope: Level annuities-immediate a_n| and annuities-due a_dot_n|: derivations of present values and accumulated values s_n| and s_dot_n|
Continuous annuities bar_a_n| and annuities payable m-thly a_n|^(m): mathematical relationships and expansions
Deferred annuities m|a_n| and perpetuities a_infinity| and a_dot_infinity|
Arithmetically increasing annuities (Ia)_n| and decreasing annuities (Da)_n|: algebraic derivations and summation formulas
Geometrically increasing annuities and continuous varying annuities with polynomial payment rates
Loan amortization schedules: outstanding balance calculation via prospective and retrospective methods, principal and interest decomposition, and sinking funds

units.title: Survival Models, Life Tables & Parametric Mortality Laws
scope: Continuous future lifetime random variable T_x for a life aged x: survival function S_x(t) = t_p_x, cumulative mortality probability t_q_x
Force of mortality (hazard rate) mu_x+t: definition, relationship to survival probability t_p_x = exp(- integral_0^t mu_x+s ds)
Curtate future lifetime K_x = floor(T_x): probability mass function, relation to complete lifetime, and expectation of life e_x and e_circle_x
Parametric laws of mortality: de Moivre's linear law, Gompertz's exponential law mu_x = B c^x, Makeham's law mu_x = A + B c^x, and Weibull law
Construction and structure of life tables: radix l_0, cohort survival numbers l_x, deaths d_x, central death rates m_x, and fractional age assumptions (UDD, CFM)
Select, ultimate, and aggregate life tables: underwriting selection effects, duration-dependent mortality, and table graduation techniques

units.title: Life Insurance Contracts & Actuarial Present Value Valuations
scope: Stochastic present value loss variable Z for life insurance contracts payable at the moment of death or at the end of the year of death
Continuous whole life insurance bar_A_x: Actuarial Present Value (APV / net single premium), integral formulation, and second moment ^2 bar_A_x
Discrete whole life insurance A_x: derivation using commutation functions and summation over life table cohorts
Term insurance contracts bar_A_x:n|^1 and A_x:n|^1: net single premium formulas and expiration without value
Pure endowment contracts A_x:n|^E = n_E_x = v^n n_p_x and endowment insurance contracts A_x:n| = A_x:n|^1 + n_E_x
Deferred insurances, varying insurance benefits (increasing whole life (IA)_x), and m-thly payable death benefits A_x^(m)

units.title: Life Annuities: Continuous, Discrete, Varying & Guaranteed Contracts
scope: Stochastic present value random variable Y for life annuities: continuous whole life annuity bar_a_x and discrete annuity-due a_dot_x
Fundamental equivalence relations between life insurances and life annuities: A_x = 1 - d a_dot_x and bar_A_x = 1 - delta bar_a_x
Temporary life annuities bar_a_x:n| and a_dot_x:n|: integral and summation formulas, and relations to endowment insurance
Deferred life annuities u|a_x and guaranteed life annuities with a term-certain minimum payout period a_x:k|
Life annuities payable m-thly a_dot_x^(m): Woolhouse's formula and uniform distribution of deaths approximations
Varying life annuities: arithmetically increasing life annuities (I a_dot)_x and continuous increasing annuities (I bar_a)_x

units.title: Benefit Premiums, the Equivalence Principle & Loss-at-Issue Variance
scope: The Equivalence Principle: setting net level annual premiums so that the expected present value of future benefits equals expected future premiums E[_0L] = 0
Net level premiums for standard policies: whole life P_x = A_x / a_dot_x, term P_x:n|^1, pure endowment P_x:n|^E, and endowment insurance P_x:n|
Continuous benefit premiums bar_P(bar_A_x) and premiums payable m-thly P_x^(m)
Variance of the future loss-at-issue random variable Var(_0L) for discrete and continuous policies under the equivalence principle
The Percentile Premium Principle: setting premiums to bound the probability of ruin/loss P(_0L > 0) <= alpha
Gross premiums: incorporating initial expenses, renewal expenses, claim settlement costs, and profit loadings into the equation of value

units.title: Benefit Reserves, Thiele's Differential Equation & Expense Loadings
scope: The necessity of policy reserves: level premium payment schedules vs age-increasing hazard rates and mortality costs
Prospective benefit reserves _t V: definition as expected present value of future benefits minus expected future net premiums
Retrospective benefit reserves _t V: definition as accumulated past net premiums minus accumulated past claims; proof of equivalence
Recursive reserve relationships for discrete policies: (_t V + P)(1+i) = q_x+t + p_x+t _t+1 V, and net amount at risk (death strain)
Continuous reserves and Thiele's Differential Equation: d/dt _t V = delta _t V + P - mu_x+t (1 - _t V)
Expense reserves: modified reserve systems (Full Preliminary Term / FPT, Commissioners Reserve Valuation Method / CRVM) and surrender values

units.title: Mathematical Demography, Multiple Decrement Models & Population Dynamics
scope: Multiple decrement theory: competing risks, cause-specific forces of mortality mu_x^(j), crude, net, and partial net decrement probabilities
Construction of multiple decrement tables: associated single decrement tables under constant force and uniform distribution assumptions
Joint life status T_xy and last survivor status T_xy_bar: survival functions, independence, and covariance between statuses
Stable population theory: Alfred Lotka's integral renewal equation B(t) = integral_0^infinity B(t-a) p(a) m(a) da and intrinsic rate of natural increase r
Stationary population models: relationship between life expectancy e_0, birth rate, death rate, and age composition
Discrete population projection models: the Leslie Matrix model, dominant eigenvalues, stable age distributions, and demographic momentum
